1. (Currently amended) A coupling system configured to secure one or more struts to a wing of an aircraft, the coupling system comprising:
one or more splice straps that secure the one or more struts to the wing,
one or more mounting plates configured to span over or below the one or more struts and the wing, wherein the one or more mounting plates are configured to provide a base on which one or more of the splice straps securely mount to one or both the one or more struts or the wing, and wherein the one or more of the splice straps are secured directly to one or more ribs of the wing.
2. (Currently amended) The coupling system of claim 1, wherein the one or more splice straps are integrally formed with the one or more struts and the wing.
3. (Original) The coupling system of claim 1, wherein a rear surface of the one or more struts are linearly aligned with a front surface of a front spar of the wing.
4. (Original) The coupling system of claim 3, wherein an engine is secured to the one or more struts distally from the wing.
5. (Currently amended) The coupling system of claim 1, wherein the one or more splice straps secure to both the one or more struts and the one or more ribs of the wing.
6. (Currently amended) The coupling system of claim 5, wherein the one or more splice straps comprise:
one or more upper splice straps extending over a first top surface of a rear end of the one or more struts and a second top surface of a front end of the one or more ribs; and
one or more lower splice straps extending over a first bottom surface of the rear end of the one or more struts and a second bottom surface of the front end of the one or more ribs.
7. (Original) The coupling system of claim 6, wherein the one or more upper splice straps comprise a first upper splice strap and a second upper splice strap, and wherein the one or
more lower splice straps comprise a first lower splice strap and a second lower splice strap.
8. (Original) The coupling system of claim 7, wherein the one or more upper splice straps further comprise a third upper splice strap between the first upper splice strap and the second upper splice strap, and wherein the one or more lower splice straps further comprise a third lower splice strap between the first lower splice strap and the second lower splice strap.
9. (Currently amended) The coupling system of claim 5, wherein the one more splice straps are vertically and longitudinally aligned with the one or more struts and the one or more ribs.
10. (Currently amended) The coupling system of claim 1, further comprising one or more fairings covering at least a portion of the one or more splice straps.
11. (Currently amended) The coupling system of claim 1, wherein the one or more mounting plates are between the one or more splice straps and the one or more struts, and between the one or more splice straps and the wing.
12. (Currently amended) The coupling system of claim 1, further comprising one or more spanning plates configured to span across the one or more a plurality of ribs, wherein the one or more splice straps are coupled to the one or more spanning plates.
13. (Currently amended) A method for securing one or more struts to a wing of an aircraft, the method comprising:
securing, by one or more splice straps, the one or more struts to the wing,
providing, by one or more mounting plates that span over or below the one or more struts and the wing, provide a base on which one or more of the splice straps securely mount to one or both the one or more struts or the wing; and
securing the one or more of the splice straps to one or more ribs of the wing.
14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein said securing comprises integrally forming the one or more splice straps with the one or more struts and the wing.
15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein said securing comprises securing the one or more splice straps to both the one or more struts and the one or more ribs of the wing.
16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 15, wherein the one or more splice straps comprise:
one or more upper splice straps extending over a first top surface of a rear end of the one or more struts and a second top surface of a front end of the one or more ribs; and
one or more lower splice straps extending over a first bottom surface of the rear end of the one or more struts and a second bottom surface of the front end of the one or more ribs.
17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 15, wherein said securing further comprises vertically and longitudinally aligning the one more splice straps with the one or more struts strut and the one or more ribs.
18. (Currently amended) An aircraft comprising:
a fuselage;
a wing extending from the fuselage, wherein the wing comprises a front spar and one or more ribs;
one or more struts, wherein a rear surface of the one or more struts are linearly aligned with a front surface of the front spar;
an engine secured to the one or more struts distally from the wing; and
a coupling system securing the one or more struts to the wing, the coupling system comprising:one or more splice straps that secure the one or more struts to the wing, wherein
the one or more splice straps are integrally formed with the one or more struts and the wing, wherein the one or more splice straps secure to both the one or more struts and the one or more ribs, and wherein the one or more splice straps are vertically and longitudinally aligned with the one or more struts and the one or more ribs,
wherein the one or more splice straps comprise:one or more upper splice straps extending over a first top surface of a rear end of the one or more struts and a second top surface of a front end of the one or more ribs, wherein the one or more upper splice straps comprise a first upper splice strap, a second upper splice strap, and a third upper splice strap between the first upper splice strap and the second upper splice strap; and
one or more lower splice straps extending over a first bottom surface of the rear end of the one or more struts and a second bottom surface of the front end of the one or more ribs, wherein the one or more lower splice straps comprise a first lower splice strap, a second lower splice strap, and a third lower splice strap between the first lower splice strap and the second lower splice strap; and
an upper mounting plate spanning over the one or more struts and the wing, wherein the upper mounting plate provide a base on which the first upper splice strap, the second upper splice strap, and the third upper splice strap securely mount to the one or more struts and the wing, wherein the first upper splice strap is secured directly over a first rib, and wherein the second upper splice strap is securely directly over a second rib; and
a lower mounting plate spanning below the one or more struts and the wing, wherein the lower mounting plate provides a base on which the first lower splice strap, the second lower splice strap, and the third lower splice strap securely mount to the one or more struts and the wing, wherein the first lower splice strap is secured directly under the first rib, and wherein the second lower splice strap is secured directly under the second rib.

22. (Currently amended) The coupling system of claim 1, further comprising:
a first lateral brace secured to a first outer lateral surface of the one or more struts and a front spar of the wing; and
a second lateral brace secured to a second outer lateral surface of the one or more struts and the front spar of the wing, wherein the second outer lateral surface is opposite from the first lateral surface.
23. (New) The method of claim 13, further comprising:
securing a first lateral brace to a first outer lateral surface of the one or more struts and a front spar of the wing; and
securing a second lateral brace to a second outer lateral surface of the one or more struts and the front spar of the wing, wherein the second outer lateral surface is opposite from the first lateral surface.
24. (New) The aircraft of claim 18, wherein the coupling system, further comprises:
a first lateral brace secured to a first outer lateral surface of the one or more struts and a front spar of the wing; and
a second lateral brace secured to a second outer lateral surface of the one or more struts and the front spar of the wing, wherein the second outer lateral surface is opposite from the first lateral surface.
